questions.prompt: Order the four phases that make up LCP.

items.text: Resource load delay (before the LCP resource starts loading)
Resource load time (the LCP resource downloads)

questions.explanation: LCP = TTFB + resource load delay + resource load time + element render delay. Diagnosing which phase dominates points you to the right fix.

questions.prompt: Why should you never add loading="lazy" to the LCP image?

options.text: Because lazy loading corrupts the image
Because it delays loading the very element LCP measures, making LCP worse
Because lazy loading only works on videos
Because it increases the image's file size

questions.explanation: loading="lazy" defers an image until it's about to scroll into view. The LCP image is already in view and should load eagerly — lazy-loading it directly worsens LCP.

questions.prompt: Match each slow LCP phase to the fix that targets it.

pairs.right: Use a CDN and cache at the edge
Preload the image and make it discoverable in the HTML
Use a modern format and correct dimensions

questions.explanation: Each phase has a matching fix: CDN for TTFB, early discovery/preload for load delay, image optimization for load time, and removing render-blocking resources for render delay.

questions.prompt: The HTML attribute that hints a resource should be fetched at high priority is ____ (write it as attribute=value).
questions.explanation: fetchpriority="high" raises a fetch's priority. On the LCP image it helps the browser download it ahead of less important resources.

questions.prompt: Which techniques help the LCP image start downloading earlier? Select all that apply.

options.text: Put it as a real in the initial HTML

questions.explanation: Being in the HTML makes it discoverable, preload starts it early, and fetchpriority raises its priority. loading="lazy" would do the opposite and delay it.

questions.prompt: If the LCP element is a block of text, what most commonly delays it?

options.text: A slow-loading web font and/or render-blocking CSS
The number of images elsewhere on the page

questions.explanation: For text LCP the 'resource' is effectively the font and CSS, so a slow web font or render-blocking CSS delays the text from painting.
